authoredNote: Expectations written from the Svelte 5 language rules for `{@render}` (the tag names a snippet and evaluates an argument list) and from the corpus files named in the fixture header; the line pins were then read off the post-fix run and each checked against the fixture's own text — `{@render row(alpha)}` on 38, the multiline list puts `beta` on 41 and `gamma` on 42, `{@render row(pick(delta))}` on 45, `{@render row(obj.eps)}` on 47.
rationale: JOB 2 of the svelte ontology pass. `{@render tag(args)}` is a call AND an argument evaluation; the template pass scanned the opaque render-tag text for a callable name and stopped, so the argument reads were silent. Corpus measurement: 126 argumented render tags across 83 of the 6,439 .svelte files published zero reads, while the identical name in a mustache in the same file does publish one. The callee stays owned by `calls` — a `uses` at the callee would double-count one fact as two — and a member LEAF is skipped by the collector's own dot rule, so `{@render row(obj.eps)}` contributes `obj` and not `eps`. The multiline form is pinned at the IDENTIFIER's line because the naive base line claims the tag's own line, which is the M59 (#825) rule this lane already follows for every other template read. Each argument has its own member name because the collector's read map is keyed by NAME: two reads of one name collapse to the last site, so a line pin on a repeated name would assert a property this lane does not have.

forbidRelationships.comment: a member LEAF is not a member read: `obj.eps` reads `obj`. The collector's dot rule has always skipped these; pinning it here is what stops a future widening from publishing `eps`.
the CALLEE belongs to the `calls` edge. A `uses` at the callee would double-count one fact as two.
the snippet PARAMETER is a template-local binding, never a member read — the S5 shadow case, and the control that a render-tag argument sweep did not simply read the whole fragment
the multiline argument's base line must advance to the identifier's own line (41), not stay on the tag's line — the M59 #825 rule this lane already follows for every other template read
`gamma` is the SECOND argument; its line is 42, never the first argument's
